#Text=Can you describe the content of this map?
#Text=The image is a screenshot of a Google Maps interface, showing a section of Paris, France.
#Text=The map highlights several streets and landmarks:  Avenue Blaise Pascal runs horizontally across the left side.
#Text=Boulevard Descartes intersects with Avenue Blaise Pascal on the left.
#Text=Boulevard Corot is visible in the center-right area.
#Text=Avenue André-Marie Ampère, which runs vertically, is located to the right of Boulevard Corot.

#Text=Key points of interest marked include:  Université Gustave Eiffel: Located near the intersection of Avenue Blaise Pascal and Boulevard Descartes. d.school Paris (part of École des Ponts Paristech): Situated on Boulevard Corot, close to its intersection with Boulevard Descartes.
#Text=École d’Urbanisme de Paris: Positioned at the bottom center near Boulevard Corot.

#Text=There are also several businesses and establishments marked: - Les Lumières (likely a restaurant or café) is located in the upper central area. - O’Poké, another establishment, is nearby Les Lumières. - Addictiss Café: Situated further to the right of O’Poké.
#Text=Other points include residential areas and other establishments like “Le Trois Quatorze” (a restaurant or café) near Boulevard Corot.

#Text=Buildings and Locations: Certain buildings or locations, like the “École d’Urbanisme de Paris” (School of Urbanism), are marked with a small icon that resembles a building, making them easily identifiable as significant points on the map.

#Text=The combination of these elements—labeled roads and streets, building icons, points of interest markers, institution labels, and service icons—makes the map informative and visually engaging.
